research_scope: Six context-checked aliases: polynomial evaluation homomorphism family, kernel of commutative ring homomorphism, and a field-polynomial notation into the existing polynomial algebra canonical candidate.

aliases.reason: The four phrases refer to the unique coefficient-preserving evaluation homomorphism from a polynomial ring into a specified commutative R-algebra; a polynomial's value f(α) is its evaluation-map image, and sending X_s to s yields the same universal evaluation construction. Different targets, variable sets and surjectivity claims remain separate source conditions. Original phrase 'polynomial evaluation f(α) at element of E' compared to canonical 'evaluation homomorphism k[X_i:i∈I]→K'; no contextual homonym is being merged.

The source refers in each case to the kernel ideal of a unital commutative-ring homomorphism: elements of the source ring sent to additive zero. One source evaluates polynomials, another evaluates an arbitrary-index polynomial algebra, and a third composes localization and quotient. The kernel concept is the same; equality with a specified contraction remains additional source content. Original phrase 'kernel of R→R_p/p^nR_p' compared to canonical 'I=ker(P→S)'; no contextual homonym is being merged.

A univariate F[x] is the same general finitely supported commutative unital polynomial algebra as the indexed R[X_i]; the choice of field as coefficient ring and singleton index set specializes, rather than changes, this general prerequisite. The original field-extension definition continues to specify evaluation of the polynomial at α separately; no evaluation-specific meaning is collapsed with the polynomial algebra.
